newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki operators have appetite for issues, IPOs.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki operators have appetite for issues, IPOs.

text.p: Strong demand for share issues and introductions on the Helsinki stock exchange may well propel the amount of 1997 issues to exceed last year's 4.8 billion markka, fund managers and analysts said on Monday.

The sentiment remains positive on the Helsinki market despite rampant gains in the first months of the year -- the HEX general index has added about 20 percent in a record-breaking streak -- and the liquid bourse has capacity to absorb new shares, they said.
"At the moment it is hard to see how there could be too many issues," said Matti Rusanen, fund manager with Gyllenberg.

On the supply side, though most Finnish firms are well capitalised and some more likely to buy back shares once they are allowed to in September rather than issue new ones, the state's need for money will ensure some supply, Rusanen added.
The 1997 state budget includes one billion markka in privatisation income.

For fund managers, this year's highlights would be the planned offerings of state power producer Imatran Voima (IVO) and Helsinki telephone operator Helsingin Puhelin Oy, said managing director Kai Luotonen at Selin Funds.
"It would be important in the medium term from the point of view of cyclicality to get listed public utilities and tele-operators, which are typically not very cyclical," Luotonen said.

He said many investors fear a stock market correction at some stage this year and the best timing for issues would be when the market is rallying after a correction -- but the consensus view was that issues would be welcome sooner rather than later.
"It would be good to see issues before the market loses steam," said Rusanen.
"If (issuers) only had the time, the spring would be a better time," said Evli fund manager Henrik Damsten.

Other expected newcomers apart from Helsingin Puhelin and IVO are cable maker PK-Cables and Aktia Bank. Design textile maker Marimekko's owner Kirsti Paakkanen said in an interview published on Friday that she had listing plans too.

Only two share issues have so far been announced for this year. They are engineering firm Santasalo's 600,000 shares and capital notes for 75 million markka, and construction group YIT's issue of 4.0 million shares to boost its balance sheet.
Rautaruukki on Friday asked for issue authorisation and analysts expect the steel group to make a move soon. The state is free to lower its 69 percent holding to 33 percent in Rautaruukki.

"There are some other state-owned companies also waiting for privatisation, so I expect they have to have Rautaruukki issue soon, probably before next summer," FSB analyst Jukka Fransas told Reuters on Friday.
FIM Securities analysts Niklas Geust said bourse dividend payouts also speak for a near-term timing for Rautaruukki.
"Spring and early summer would be good time for an issue since there is dividend money available," he said.
Evli's Damsten and Gyllenberg's Rusanen also foresaw activity in oil and chemicals group Neste.
Rusanen expected a share issue to finance a service shut-down at Neste's Porvoo refinery and a state sale of some of its 84 percent holding, but Damsten did not expect new shares to be issued.

"I think there can be a state sale in the autumn when Neste has one good four-month report behind them," he said, adding that the market could absorb some 18 percent of the state's holding of Neste's stock, so that would fall to two-thirds.
